case_name: Ashok Yadav and Others v State of Madhya Pradesh
respondent:
State of Madhya Pradesh
Supreme Court of India

19 November 1996
Appeal (Crl.) 58-59 of 1995
The Order of the Court was as follows :
1.  These appeals are directed against the judgment of the High Court of Madhya Pradesh dated 8th April, 1994 dismissing the appeals filed by the appellants against their conviction and sentence as recorded by the learned Sessions Judge on 18fh January, 1991. The appellants were convicted of offences under sections 364 and 302 IPC and were sentenced to five years rigorous imprisonment and to pay a fine of Rs. 500 and in default two months simple imprisonment on the first count and to life imprisonment and a fine of Rs. 1,000 and in default three months simple imprisonment on the second count.
2.  The prosecution case in brief is that on 2nd September, 1987 at about 9.15 p.m., Ramgovind Sharma, PW. 9 lodged a report at P.S. Jhansi Road regarding the missing of his son Avadhesh Sharma who had gone to .the school but had not returned
facts: The Order of the Court was as follows :
The appellants were convicted of offences under sections 364 and 302 IPC
Ramgovind Sharma, PW.9 lodged a report at P.S. Jhansi Road regarding the missing of his son Avadhesh Sharma
A search was made for the appellants.
They were not found at their houses.
A case under section 364/34 IPC was registered on 3rd September, 1987 at 1 O' Clock at night.
The dead body of Avadesh was found between the bushes and trees in the Chattri.
Dr. V.K, Deewan, P.W. conducted the post-mortem examination and found a number of injuries on his person.
Gauri Shankar, appellant, is alleged to have made a disclosure statement which is admissible under section 27 of the Evidence Act leading to the recovery of a watch

Mohan, appellant, allegedly made a statement admissible under section 27 of the Evidence Act leading to the recovery of a pen while Veerandra, appellant, allegedly made a statement admissible under Section 27 of the Evidence Act leading to the recovery of a dot pen.

The recovered articles were sent to the police station for identification and Shri B.K. Agrawal, Naib Tahsildar, PW.11 conducted an identification parade in the Tehsil Office of Gwalior on 18th September, 1987.
issues: Whether the prosecution has established beyond a reasonable doubt that the appellants had committed the murder of Avadhesh.
Whether the recoveries of articles are genuine and reliable.
Whether the evidence of absconding is consistent with the hypothesis of guilt of the appellants.
respondent_arguments: The prosecution has led sufficient evidence to connect the appellants with the crime.
The motive for murder was established through the evidence of PW.9 and PW.10.
The recoveries of articles were genuine and reliable.
The evidence of absconding was consistent with the hypothesis of guilt of the appellants.
court_reasoning: This circumstance, has in our opinion, not been proved and even otherwise, it does not appear that there was any sufficient motive for the appellants to commit the murder of the only son of PW.9, only because PW.9 had to appear as a witness against the brother of Ashok, appellant.
The recoveries are not free from doubt and the same appear to have been pressed into aid to buttress the prosecution's case.

The evidence of Parmal Singh, PW.6, when considered in the established facts and circumstances of the case, creates a doubt about his crediworthiness and consequently about the genuineness of the recoveries.

The arrest of the appellants on 6th September, 1987 when the case was registered under section 364/34 IPC only during the night intervening 3rd/4th September, 1987, cannot be considered to be such a circumstance which connects the appellants with the murder of the deceased and is consistent only with the hypothesis of the guilt of the appellants.

The evidence led by the prosecution about 'last seen together' cannot be said to be consistent only with the hypothesis of the guilt of the appellants as regards the offence of murder and incapable of being explained on any other hypothesis.
holding: The conviction of the appellants for the offence under section 302 IPC, therefore, cannot be sustained and is hereby set aside.

So far as the conviction of the appellants for offence under Section 364 IPC is concerned, that too cannot be sustained because the kidnapping of the deceased by the appellants cannot be said to be with the intention to commit his murder.
